title: Maxwell–Boltzmann distribution
examples: How does temperature affect the average speed of gas particles?
Can a catalyst change the shape of the distribution curve?
What does the peak of the curve represent in terms of molecular energy?

explain.say: The Maxwell-Boltzmann distribution shows particle speeds.
The curve shows the fraction of molecules at different speeds.
Increasing the temperature increases the average speed of molecules.
A catalyst changes the activation energy, not the curve shape.
The curve spreads out and the peak lowers at higher temperatures.
In a real gas reaction, higher temperature means faster collisions.

faq.q: Does the distribution curve change if I change the gas?
faq.a: No, the shape depends on temperature, not the type of gas. It only depends on the gas's molar mass and temperature.
asks: Does mass matter for the curve?
Is the curve specific to the gas type?

faq.q: If I increase the temperature, does the average speed increase proportionally?
faq.a: The root mean square speed increases with the square root of the absolute temperature. It does not increase directly with temperature.
asks: How does T affect average speed?
Is the speed increase linear with temperature?

faq.q: Can a catalyst change the shape of the Maxwell-Boltzmann curve?
faq.a: No, a catalyst only lowers the activation energy needed for the reaction to occur. It does not change the distribution of speeds.
asks: Does a catalyst affect the curve shape?
What is the catalyst's effect on energy?

faq.q: What does the peak of the curve represent?
faq.a: The peak represents the most probable speed for the molecules at that specific temperature. This is the speed most molecules possess.
asks: What is the most common speed?

faq.q: Does pressure affect the distribution curve?
faq.a: Pressure changes the frequency of collisions, but it does not change the shape of the Maxwell-Boltzmann distribution curve itself.
asks: Is pressure related to the curve?
Does P change the speed distribution?

facts: The distribution curve shows the relative number of molecules at speeds.
Increasing the temperature increases the average kinetic energy of the gas.
A catalyst lowers the activation energy, speeding up the rate.
The shape of the curve depends on temperature and gas type.

quiz.say: If you increase the temperature of a gas, what happens to the curve?
quiz.show: The curve becomes wider and the peak lowers.

options.show: The curve remains exactly the same shape.
options.say: The curve remains exactly the same shape.

options.show: The curve becomes wider and the peak lowers.
options.say: The curve becomes wider and the peak lowers.

options.show: The curve shifts to the right.
options.say: The curve shifts to the right.

quiz.why: Higher temperature means more energy, so more speeds are possible, spreading the curve out.

wrong.0: The shape changes because the average kinetic energy of the gas increases.
wrong.2: This suggests a constant increase in speed for all molecules, which is incorrect.
wrong.3: This implies that more molecules suddenly gain the most probable speed, which is not the case.

quiz.say: What is the primary effect of a catalyst on a reaction?

options.show: Shifting the entire curve to higher speeds.
options.say: Shifting the entire curve to higher speeds.

quiz.why: Catalysts provide an alternative reaction pathway with less energy required.

wrong.0: The catalyst affects the energy barrier, not the inherent speed distribution.
wrong.2: This describes the effect of temperature, not a catalyst.
wrong.3: Catalysts do not change the physical identity or mass of the reactants.

quiz.say: If you compare two gases at the same temperature, which gas has the higher average speed?
quiz.show: Lighter gas has higher average speed.

options.show: Lighter gas has higher average speed.
options.say: Lighter gas has higher average speed.

options.show: The gas with the larger molar mass.
options.say: The gas with the larger molar mass.

options.show: The gas that is more reactive.
options.say: The gas that is more reactive.

quiz.why: At the same temperature, the average kinetic energy is equal, meaning lighter molecules move faster.

wrong.0: Pressure affects collision frequency, not the average speed at constant temperature.
wrong.2: Mass is inversely related to speed at constant temperature.
wrong.3: Reactivity is not directly related to the average speed of particles.
